title: Hold your price, handle discounts and check your numbers
course_title: Pricing & Value Strategy for Services and Digital Work

say: Hold your price, handle discounts, and check your numbers.
This is the video for Module 3 of Pricing and Value Strategy.
Many women calculate a good price, then give it away in the first minute. 'It is 70,000 naira, but I can reduce it' invites the client to ask for less.
So say the price as a fact, link it to what is included, and wait. Silence is normal. The client is thinking.

say: For example, a fashion brand in Kaduna asks Zainab, 'Can you do 50,000 naira?' She thanks them and stays calm.

say: She asks which part matters most: the posts, the catalogue updates or the report.

say: Option one is a smaller scope: the Basic package at 58,000 naira.

say: Option two is better terms: Standard at 66,000 naira a month, for three months paid upfront. Still above her floor. The owner chooses option two, and Zainab confirms it in writing.

say: Ask for something of value in return: less scope, a longer commitment, payment upfront or a longer deadline. If no option reaches your floor, decline politely. Losing a below-floor job is not a loss.

panel.rule: Never give a price cut without getting something back.

say: For projects, take a deposit, for example 50%, and the balance before you release final files. Retainers are paid at the start of each month.
Put a due date on every invoice, and say what happens if payment is late: a reminder, a second reminder after 3 days, and work paused after 7 days overdue.
Always confirm payment in your own banking app, never from a screenshot alone.

panel.heading: Write these into every quote
items: Projects: deposit first, balance before files
Retainers: paid at the start of the month
A due date on every invoice
Late payment steps, then work paused
Confirm payments in your banking app

say: Costs rise and your skill grows, so prices must move too. For example, Zainab has served a pharmacy for 18 months at 60,000 naira. That is only 2,600 naira above her floor.

panel.heading: A fair increase after 18 months
items: Start date at least 30 days away

say: She decides on a 15% increase, to 69,000 naira.

panel.heading: A fair increase after 18 months

say: She gives at least 30 days' notice, so the client can plan.

say: The pharmacy accepts. Her margin on this client rises to 11,600 naira.

say: Track hours for every client, including messages and calls. Then calculate the effective hourly rate and the margin above floor. Zainab's Client A pays 70,000 naira, but the work took 18 hours. That is below her floor.

say: And she billed only 64 of her 88 hours. With Client D on Basic and one more Standard client, her income would reach 366,000 naira, above her target.
A big client can still be a poor client. Look at margin above floor, not just the size of the payment.
